description: Decision 93 coastal-node rule (user decision 2026-10-17 on S4D_STOP_01_COASTAL_NODES.md (chat): option A, corrected to the physical coastline consistent with the 'not-land' reading of supplement 01): a node is coastal when its onshore region touches the physical coast (any sea, internal and archipelagic waters included, e.g. the Bight of Bangkok and the Cambodian coast; not the EEZ alone), or a sea port / LNG terminal is recorded at it; river-only ports do not count; converter nodes within 5 km of the sea are coastal. Reason: the IEAGHG (2004) ship cost already contains port, buffer tanks and loading facilities, so a coast is enough to build a CO2 loading terminal; river ports are excluded for lack of draught. Re-judged: TH2 2 inland (only the Bangkok river port; its region stops 7.3 km from the Bight, the strip belongs to TH2 3), KH2 4 inland (region 44 km from the sea, the land between is TH2 3)
